bottom_line: The ratings were made before or during a rout that hit the worldview's own named risks (data-centre policy, crowded trade), and every name except PWR is 6-33% below its rated price. Futures bounce, but the October jobs report lands around the open and traders price a December rate hike, so I would let the open settle before acting.
what_changed: Nasdaq fell 5.5% on Thursday, its worst day since April 2025, and the semis ETF fell 11.2%: this is the political-risk-to-data-centres thesis playing out.
Friday pre-market: Nasdaq-100 futures +1% to +1.7%, S&P 500 +0.3-0.4%, Dow futures -0.9%; AMD, Intel, Broadcom and Micron up 5-8% early.
October payrolls are due about the open (consensus roughly 59,000-65,000 jobs, 4.2% unemployment); CME FedWatch shows a more than 65% chance of a December hike, which touches the high-rates thesis.
Brent and WTI slipped below $100 a barrel, easing one of the worldview's inflation risks.

names.take: Segment is neutral in the worldview; cheaper than when rated, but wait for the jobs-day open.
Down 13% since rating with a neutral segment; the rating predates the rout, so treat it as stale.

Segment still overweight, but earnings come on Monday; wait for the print.
Freshest rating and an overweight segment, but the agents saw the post-rout price; a limit order is safer at a volatile open.
Worldview now rates memory underweight and the stock is down a third since rating: the two disagree, and I'd trust the worldview tonight.
Segment overweight, but Vertiv fell 14% in a day and the permitting risk is live; small size only, after the open settles.

trust: 33 picks have been made and none are graded yet (grading starts after 28 days). So far the picks average -10.9% against QQQ, and only the Screen's #1, the random pick and the whole universe are worse or similar, so the ratings have not earned trust yet.
if_buying: Overweight means a small starter position only, not a full one.
Wait on ASML, DELL, STX and NRG: the first three are stale and well below their rated prices, and NRG reports on Monday.
If you act, prefer PWR or VRT, where the segment still matches the worldview, with limit orders because the open is likely to swing on payrolls.
Overnight news was checked through Friday morning only; no payroll figure was available.
